summary_html: Child achieves **permanency through legal guardianship** or kinship care. Federal programs provide funding parity with adoption for approved relatives.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that a third party seeking custody over a fit parent's objection must plead and prove, by a fair preponderance, that continued parental custody would be clearly damaging, injurious or harmful to the child, and that such awards are justified only in exceptional circumstances.
key_cases.relevance: It is the leading Connecticut statement of the harm standard and burden of proof for third-party guardianship and custody permanency.
key_cases.quote: the petitioner must allege and prove, at the very least, that continued parental custody will be clearly damaging, injurious or harmful to the child

key_cases.holding: The court held § 46b-59 unconstitutional as applied where visitation was ordered over a fit parent's objection without any allegation and proof by clear and convincing evidence of a parent-like relationship and of actual, significant harm to the children if visitation were denied, and it reversed with direction to dismiss the petition.
key_cases.relevance: Together with Fish v. Fish it is the controlling Connecticut harm standard and burden of proof constraining any third-party or kinship permanency arrangement.
key_cases.quote: The petition must also contain specific, good faith allegations that denial of the visitation will cause real and significant harm to the child.

key_cases.holding: The court held that a parent who shows the factors that caused her removal as guardian have been satisfactorily resolved is entitled to a presumption that reinstatement of guardianship is in the child's best interests, which the opposing party must rebut by clear and convincing evidence.
key_cases.relevance: It defines the standard for undoing a guardianship permanency arrangement under § 45a-611.
key_cases.quote: We also conclude that the party opposing reinstatement must rebut this presumption by clear and convincing evidence.

key_cases.holding: The court dismissed the appeal, holding that a relative seeking the child had no colorable claim to intervene as of right in the termination proceeding, so denial of her motion was not an appealable final judgment.
key_cases.relevance: A relative hoping for guardianship cannot obtain party status as of right in the termination proceeding that precedes permanency.
key_cases.quote: Thus, we conclude that Maria G. has failed to plead a colorable claim to intervene as of right.

key_cases.holding: The court held that § 46b-129 (p), which gives foster parents a right to be heard and comment, does not prohibit a trial court from permitting foster parents to intervene in neglect proceedings, rejecting the contrary rule of In re Ryan C., and reversed.
key_cases.relevance: Foster and preadoptive caregivers may be permitted to intervene and press a competing permanency position, including on revocation of commitment.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the statute does not prohibit a trial court from permitting foster parents to intervene in such proceedings.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: A four-Justice plurality held Washington's third-party visitation statute unconstitutional as applied because the trial court gave no special weight to a fit mother's own determination of her daughters' best interests, there being a presumption that fit parents act in their children's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: Any third-party guardianship or kinship permanency arrangement must give special weight to the fit parent's own determination before it can be imposed.
key_cases.quote: if a fit parent's decision of the kind at issue here becomes subject to judicial review, the court must accord at least some special weight to the parent's own determination
